arxiv-1901-09290.title: PruneTrain : Fast Neural Network Training by Dynamic Sparse Model Reconfiguration Conference: The International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage, and Analysis; November 17–22, 2019; Denver, CO, USA The International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking,
arxiv-1901-09290.creator: Sangkug Lym, Esha Choukse, Siavash Zangeneh, Wei Wen, Sujay Sanghavi, Mattan Erez
arxiv-1901-09290.description: Abstract . State-of-the-art convolutional neural networks (CNNs) used in vision applications have large models with numerous weights. Training these models is very compute- and memory-resource intensive. Much research has been done on pruning or compressing these models to reduce the cost of inference, but little work has addressed the costs of training. We focus precisely on accelerating training.

arxiv-2101-05974.title: Inductive Representation Learning in Temporal Networks via Causal Anonymous Walks
arxiv-2101-05974.creator: Yanbang Wang, Yen-Yu Chang, Yunyu Liu, Jure Leskovec, Pan Li
arxiv-2101-05974.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yanbang Wang, Yen-Yu Chang, Yunyu Liu, Jure Leskovec, Pan Li. Temporal networks serve as abstractions of many real-world dynamic systems. These networks typically evolve according to certain laws, such as the law of triadic closure, which is universal in social networks. Inductive representation learning of temporal networks should be able to capture such laws and further be applied to systems that follow the same laws but have not been unseen during the training stage.

arxiv-2109-03257.title: The effects of self-interacting dark matter on the stripping of galaxies that fall into clusters 2020 The effects of self-interacting dark matter on the stripping of galaxies that fall into clusters – References
arxiv-2109-03257.creator: Ellen L. Sirks, ​ Kyle A. Oman, Andrew Robertson, Richard Massey & Carlos Frenk
arxiv-2109-03257.description: Abstract We use the Cluster-EAGLE ( c-eagle ) hydrodynamical simulations to investigate the effects of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) on galaxies as they fall into clusters. We find that SIDM galaxies follow similar orbits to their Cold Dark Matter (CDM) counterparts, but end up with ∼ {\sim} 25 per cent less mass by the present day.

arxiv-2202-00599.title: Quantum Machine Learning in Finance: Time Series Forecasting
arxiv-2202-00599.creator: Dimitrios Emmanoulopoulos and Sofija Dimoska ⋆ Chief Technology Office Barclays
arxiv-2202-00599.description: Abstract We explore the efficacy of the novel use of parametrised quantum circuits (PQCs) as quantum neural networks (QNNs) for forecasting time series signals with simulated quantum forward propagation. The temporal signals consist of several sinusoidal components (deterministic signal), blended together with trends and additive noise.

arxiv-2405-07645.title: Ergodicity of skew products over typical IETs
arxiv-2405-07645.creator: F. Argentieri, P. Berk, F. Trujillo
arxiv-2405-07645.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by F. Argentieri, P. Berk, F. Trujillo. We prove the ergodicity of a class of infinite measure-preserving systems of the form T f : [ 0 , 1 ) × ℝ → [ 0 , 1 ) × ℝ ( x , t ) ↦ ( T ⁡ ( x ) , t + f ⁡ ( x ) ) , \begin{array}[]{cccc}T_{f}:&[0,1)\times\mathbb{R}&\rightarrow&[0,1)\times\mathbb{R}\\ &(x,t)&\mapsto&(T(x),t+f(x))\end{array}, where T T is an interval exchange transformation and f f is a piecewise constant function with a finite number of discontinuities.

arxiv-2504-11497.title: LLM-based AI Agent for Sizing of Analog and Mixed Signal Circuit Thanks: Chang Liu is sponsored by Peter Denyer’s Scholarship at The University of Edinburgh
arxiv-2504-11497.creator: Chang Liu, Emmanuel A. Olowe, Danial Chitnis
arxiv-2504-11497.description: Abstract The design of Analog and Mixed-Signal (AMS) integrated circuits (ICs) often involves significant manual effort, especially during the transistor sizing process. While Machine Learning techniques in Electronic Design Automation (EDA) have shown promise in reducing complexity and minimizing human intervention, they still face challenges such as numerous iterations and a lack of knowledge about AMS circuit design.

arxiv-2511-18654.title: From Healthy Scans to Annotated Tumors: A Tumor Fabrication Framework for 3D Brain MRI Synthesis
arxiv-2511-18654.creator: Nanyu Dong, Townim Chowdhury, Hieu Phan, Mark Jenkinson, Johan Verjans, Zhibin Liao
arxiv-2511-18654.description: Abstract The scarcity of annotated Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) tumor data presents a major obstacle to accurate and automated tumor segmentation. While existing data synthesis methods offer promising solutions, they often suffer from key limitations: manual modeling is labor-intensive and requires expert knowledge.

arxiv-2602-08829.title: WildReward : Learning Reward Models from In-the-Wild Human Interactions
arxiv-2602-08829.creator: Hao Peng, Yunjia Qi, Xiaozhi Wang, Zijun Yao, Lei Hou, Juanzi Li
arxiv-2602-08829.description: Abstract Reward models (RMs) are crucial for the training of large language models (LLMs), yet they typically rely on large-scale human-annotated preference pairs. With the widespread deployment of LLMs, in-the-wild interactions have emerged as a rich source of implicit reward signals. This raises the question: Can we develop reward models directly from in-the-wild interactions?

pmc-10517170.title: 3D covalent organic framework membrane with fast and selective ion transport
pmc-10517170.creator: Tianhao Zhu, Yan Kong, Bohui Lyu, Li Cao, Benbing Shi, Xiaoyao Wang, Xiao Pang, Chunyang Fan, Chao Yang, Hong Wu, Zhongyi Jiang
pmc-10517170.description: 3D ionic covalent organic framework (COF) membranes, which are envisioned to be able to break the trade-off between ion conductivity and ion selectivity, are waiting for exploitation. Herein, we report the fabrication of a 3D sulfonic acid-functionalized COF membrane (3D SCOF) for efficient and selective ion transport, using dual acid-mediated interfacial polymerization strategy.

pmc-10691731.title: The mechanism of MinD stability modulation by MinE in Min protein dynamics
pmc-10691731.creator: William C. Carlquist, Eric N. Cytrynbaum
pmc-10691731.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The patterns formed both in vivo and in vitro by the Min protein system have attracted much interest because of the complexity of their dynamic interactions given the apparent simplicity of the component parts. Despite both the experimental and theoretical attention paid to this system, the details of the biochemical interactions of MinD and MinE, the proteins responsible for the patterning, are still unclear.

pmc-11435741.title: Elimination of Human Papillomavirus 16-Positive Tumors by a Mucosal rAd5 Therapeutic Vaccination in a Pre-Clinical Murine Study
pmc-11435741.creator: Molly R. Braun, Anne C. Moore, Jonathan D. Lindbloom, Katherine A. Hodgson, Emery G. Dora, Sean N. Tucker
pmc-11435741.description: Therapeutic vaccination can harness the body’s cellular immune system to target and destroy cancerous cells. Several treatment options are available to eliminate pre-cancerous and cancerous lesions caused by human papillomaviruses (HPV), but may not result in a long-term cure. Therapeutic vaccination may offer an effective, durable, and minimally intrusive alternative.

pmc-11586047.title: The diagnostic utility of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) in the early detection of cancer: a systematic review
pmc-11586047.creator: Sarah Douglah, Reem Khalil, Reem Kanaan, Moza Almeqbaali, Nada Abdelmonem, Marc Abdelmessih, Yousr Khairalla, Natheer H. Al-Rawi
pmc-11586047.description: BackgroundGlycosaminoglycans (GAGs) are a family of polysaccharides found abundantly in the extracellular matrix (ECM) of tissues. Research has indicated that the dysregulation of ECM, including changes and disruptions in GAGs, contributes to various cancer hallmarks such as metabolic reprogramming, persistent growth signals, immunosuppression, angiogenesis, tumor invasion, and metastasis.

pmc-11692858.title: THE EFFECT OF SOCIAL PARTICIPATION OF OLDER ADULTS ON DEPRESSION: FOCUSED ON THE MODERATING EFFECT OF HOUSEHOLD TYPE
pmc-11692858.creator: Sehyun Baek, Sungkyu Lee
pmc-11692858.description: Previous studies have found that the social participation of older adults is positively associated with perceived health, happiness, and life satisfaction (Kim et al., 2018). However, as they age, their social activities tend to decrease, leading to increased depression (Choi & Kim, 2023; Kim & Jung, 2017).

pmc-12610136.title: Biomechanical Influence of Placement Angle and Loading Direction of Orthodontic Miniscrews on Orthotropic Mandible
pmc-12610136.creator: Yu-Ching Li, Jiun-Ren Hwang, Chin-Ping Fung, Chen-Yuan Chung
pmc-12610136.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). FEA of orthodontic miniscrews has predominantly assumed isotropic, homogeneous bone, neglecting directional variations in mechanical properties. This study investigated the biomechanical behavior of miniscrews under different insertion angles and loading directions using both isotropic and orthotropic mandibular bone models. The results indicated that isotropic modeling may underestimate miniscrew displacement and associated instability, whereas orthotropic material properties better reflect the true mechanical response of bone.

pmc-12627057.title: Dynamic evolution of postoperative hemodynamics in moyamoya angiopathy: a quantitative assessment of 4D Flow MRI and prognostic relevance
pmc-12627057.creator: Chao Xia, Mingzhu Fu, Rui Tian, Yutao Ren, Xu Xu, Jinge Zhang, Chunchao Xia, Chao You, Na Hu, Su Lui, Rui Li, Yi Liu
pmc-12627057.description: PurposeThe hemodynamic mechanisms underlying revascularization efficacy in moyamoya angiopathy (MMA) and their prognostic implications remain incompletely characterized. This study leverages four-dimensional flow magnetic resonance imaging (4D Flow MRI) to investigate longitudinal hemodynamic changes at the carotid siphons of MMA patients undergoing revascularization, and to evaluate their association with surgical outcomes.

pmc-12630039.title: Unraveling the impact sensitivity mechanism of energetic materials from vibrational and electronic energy transfer
pmc-12630039.creator: Wei-Hong Liu, Wei Zeng, Fu-Sheng Liu, Zheng-Tang Liu, Qi-Jun Liu
pmc-12630039.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). SummaryClarifying the sensitivity mechanism of explosives is a key prerequisite for developing energetic materials (EMs) with both low sensitivity and high detonation performance. In this study, we propose a sensitivity mechanism for energetic materials. We find that the acceleration of heat energy transfer from phonons to doorway vibrations results in a reduced transfer time to the target mode, thereby increasing the compound’s impact sensitivity.

pmc-12821259.title: Effect of body shape index trajectories on kidney disease incidence and subsequent death in individuals with type 2 diabetes
pmc-12821259.creator: Chia-Ing Li, Chiu-Shong Liu, Chih-Hsueh Lin, Shing-Yu Yang, Cheng-Chieh Lin, Tsai-Chung Li
pmc-12821259.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to identify three-year trajectories of body mass index (BMI), a body shape index (ABSI), waist circumference (WC), waist-to-hip ratio (WHR), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), and body roundness index (BRI); to assess their association with incident chronic kidney disease (CKD) and mortality; and to investigate potential sex difference in these associations.

pmc-12973268.title: Extensions to Extended Tight‐Binding Methods for Transition‐Metal Containing Systems
pmc-12973268.creator: Siyavash Moradi, Rebecca Tomann, Martin Head‐Gordon, Christopher J Stein
pmc-12973268.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Semi‐empirical quantum‐chemical methods such as extended tight‐binding (xTB) models are widely used for large‐scale simulations. Despite their popularity, their accuracy for transition‐metal containing systems is lower than, for example, closed‐shell organic molecules. In this work, we extend the Q‐Chem‐xTB framework with a geometric direct minimization (GDM) scheme for robust self‐consistent convergence and Hubbard correction (+U) to improve the description of local interactions and reduce self‐interaction errors similar to those characteristic of density‐functional theory calculations for transition‐metal complexes.

pmc-13163758.title: Sleep Architecture and Microstructure in Childhood Absence Epilepsy: Clinical and Neurophysiological Perspectives
pmc-13163758.creator: Małgorzata Jączak-Goździak, Marcin Żarowski
pmc-13163758.description: Childhood absence epilepsy (CAE) is one of the most common epilepsy syndromes in childhood and has traditionally been regarded as a condition with a favorable neurological prognosis. However, increasing evidence suggests that CAE is associated with functional disturbances in neuronal networks that extend beyond seizure generation and may involve sleep and wakefulness regulation.

pmc-13532806.title: Asthma and Multimorbidity Amongst Ethnic Minority Groups in High Income Countries
pmc-13532806.creator: Mamidipudi Thirumala Krishna, Saibal Moitra, Anna Freeman, Ben Ainsworth, Rebecca Knibb, Ramesh Kurukulaaratchy, Adel H. Mansur
pmc-13532806.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Asthma is one of the commonest noncommunicable diseases worldwide. Poor clinical outcomes have been reported in asthma amongst ethnic minority groups (EMGs) and reasons are likely to be multifactorial. There is a suggestion that underlying disease may behave differently amongst EMGs, alongside other factors including deprivation, cultural, religious, social, literacy, patient beliefs, healthcare access, treatment adherence, alongside greater burden of multimorbidity.

pmc-13621450.title: Shared evidence, different recommendations: a comparative analysis of Qdenga (TAK-003) dengue vaccine guidance for travellers across countries
pmc-13621450.creator: Sarah L McGuinness, Dipti Patel, Helena H Askling, Camilla Rothe, Steven Schofield, Robert Steffen, Leo G Visser, Lin H Chen
pmc-13621450.description: IntroductionDengue is an increasingly important cause of illness in travellers, and Qdenga (TAK-003) is the first dengue vaccine incorporated into guidance for travellers in multiple countries. However, clinicians and travellers may encounter differing recommendations across jurisdictions. This study compared guidance on the use of Qdenga in travellers across countries.
